target.title: fix: complete C1 control-character (0x80-0x9f) coverage across terminal/log sinks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Terminal-control sanitization across the codebase guards untrusted text before it reaches a terminal or log, preventing ANSI escape / log-forging injection (CWE-117). The canonical range is C0 (0x00–0x1f), DEL (0x7f), **and C1 (0x80–0x9f)** — the range already used by the shared `sanitizeForLog` in `packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.ts` and by `renderTerminalBufferText` (merged in #103274). The C1 range includes the 8-bit CSI introducer **U+009B** (equivalent to `ESC [`).

Several output sinks had drifted: they covered C0/DEL but not C1, so a C1 byte (e.g. U+009B) passed through into terminal/log output. Rather than land these as isolated one-sink patches (per maintainer feedback on #103226), this is a single **deliberate, sink-wide pass**: it audits every control-character sink, closes the C1 gap in the terminal/log output sinks, and documents why the remaining sinks are already covered, out of scope, or deferred.

## Sink-wide audit

### ① Fixed here — C1 added to terminal/log output sinks (each with a focused regression test)

| Sink (function) | File | Action on control chars |
|---|---|---|
| `hasControlCharacter` (gates `buildProviderReauthCommand`) | `src/agents/failover-error.ts` | reject (suppress command) |
| `sanitizeModelWarningValue` | `src/agents/model-selection-shared.ts` | truncate at first control |
| `hasUnsafeControlChars` | `src/agents/sandbox/runtime-status.ts` | gate (agent-only fallback) |
| `escapeControlCharsVisible` | `src/agents/tool-policy-audit.ts` | escape → `\xNN` |
| `validateAttachmentName` + `describeRejectedName` | `src/agents/subagent-attachments.ts` | reject + escape diagnostic |
| `sanitizeInlineDirectiveText` | `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.ts` | escape → `\uNNNN` |
| `scrubDoctorErrorMessage` | `src/flows/doctor-error-message.ts` | strip |
| `sanitizeLookupPathForLog` | `src/gateway/server-methods/config.ts` | replace → `?` |
| `sanitizeForConsole` | `src/agents/console-sanitize.ts` | strip |
| `escapeControlCharsForTerminal` | `src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.ts` | escape → `\xNN` |
| `replaceLogControlCharacters` (via `formatHookErrorForLog`) | `src/hooks/fire-and-forget.ts` | replace → space |
| `formatDiagnosticValue` | `src/infra/restart-handoff.ts` | replace → space |

Each keeps its own action; only the control-code classification is aligned with `sanitizeForLog`'s range. **Why not just call `sanitizeForLog`?** It strips *all* control + ANSI *and* removes tabs/newlines, and lacks these sinks' semantics — visible escaping, `?` replacement, boundary truncation, rejection, whitespace-flattening, length caps, and optional-value handling. The right boundary is the local predicate at each sink; this PR only completes the shared range there.

### ② Already C1-complete (unchanged, referenced for coverage)

- `sanitizeForLog` — `packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.ts` (canonical range).
- `renderTerminalBufferText` — `src/gateway/terminal/buffer-text.ts` (#103274, merged).

### ③ In-scope but deferred

- `sanitizeHookConsoleValue` — `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`. A console-warning sink that is genuinely in scope, but its only caller is inside the full gateway hook request handler; it warrants dedicated integration coverage. Deferred to a follow-up rather than shipping an untested one-liner here.

### ④ Considered and excluded (different threat model — not terminal/log output injection)

- `hasPromptUnsafeControlCharacter` — `src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts`: no-op for C1; the immediately-following ASCII allowlist already rejects it (this was #103401, closed).
- `stripDisallowedChatControlChars` — `src/gateway/chat-input-sanitize.ts`: chat-message **input** sanitization routed to channels; tab/LF/CR intentionally preserved.
- `sanitizeMediaDirectiveValue` — `src/agents/internal-events.ts`: builds prompt/runtime-context text, not terminal output.
- `sanitizeArgs` — `src/plugins/commands.ts`; `stripControlChars` — `src/cli/windows-argv.ts`: argv/plugin-arg normalization (input side).
- Input/URL/JSON-validity validators (`validateNoControlChars` in acp, `hasControlOrWhitespace` in scp-host, `normalizeProviderFinalUrl` in web-fetch, `isControlCharacter` in `packages/ai` JSON escaping) — reject/validate for other reasons; C1 is not an ANSI-injection concern there.

## Testing / Proof

All twelve fixed sinks have a focused regression using a **valid** U+009B sequence (CSI + `31m`, since U+009B is itself the complete introducer — no extra `[`). Per-file `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <file>` results:

| Test file | Result |
|---|---|
| `agents/failover-error.test.ts` | 98 passed (incl. C1 provider-id rejection) |
| `agents/model-selection-shared.test.ts` | 2 passed (C1 boundary truncation) |
| `agents/sandbox-explain.test.ts` | 6 passed (session-label escaping + agent-only fallback) |
| `agents/subagent-attachments.test.ts` | 3 passed (C1 name rejected + escaped diagnostic) |
| `agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts` | 57 passed |
| `agents/console-sanitize.test.ts` | 3 passed |
| `commands/doctor-state-integrity.test.ts` | 33 passed (+1 skipped) |
| `flows/doctor-error-message.test.ts` | 4 passed |
| `hooks/fire-and-forget.test.ts` | 6 passed (`formatHookErrorForLog`) |
| `infra/restart-handoff.test.ts` | 11 passed |
| `gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts` | new C1 test passes ✅ (see note) |

> Note on `config.test.ts`: four sibling `config.openFile` tests hard-code POSIX `/tmp/...` paths and assert the full path string. On my local **Windows** checkout the handler resolves those to `D:\tmp\...`, so they fail identically on `main` (unrelated to this change) and pass on Linux CI. The new `replaces C1 control characters in the logged failed config path` test deliberately asserts only the sanitized `cfg?.json` fragment, so it is green on both platforms.

Real code-point evidence (before → after) for `sanitizeModelWarningValue`, toggling only the one-line predicate: on current `main` a providerless model `gpt4<U+0080>EVIL` logs `Model "gpt4EVIL" ...` (residual C1 dropped, attacker suffix retained); with this change it logs `Model "gpt4" ...` (truncated at the C1 boundary).

## Relationship to the open C1 PRs

This supersedes the seven isolated sink PRs (#103379 #103380 #103381 #103382 #103383 #103402 #103405) and re-lands the `sanitizeForConsole` fix from the closed #103226 cleanly (valid U+009B test, no proof-only scripts). Those PRs will be closed in favor of this consolidated review.
